description.p: Kram shows every package in the enabled repositories in one table: whether it is installed, where it came from (Fedora, COPR or a third-party repository), the installed and the available version and its size. Mark packages for installation, upgrade, downgrade or removal, review the complete transaction and apply it. Nothing changes until you press Apply.

ul.li: Ranked search by name, summary, description, provided capabilities or file
Filters by status, origin, repository and comps group
Dependencies, files, versions and changelog of every package
Choose which recommended packages to install
Install a downloaded .rpm file after seeing its signature, scripts and dependencies
Enable and disable repositories, add and remove COPR projects
An optional tray icon while updates are available, without background downloads
Built on libdnf5, the library behind dnf5
A Qt window for KDE Plasma and other Qt desktops, or GTK 4 and libadwaita for GNOME (kram-gtk)

screenshot.caption: All packages with status, origin and package details
Review of the changes before applying

ul.li: The packages build again for Fedora Rawhide.
Installing kram-gtk over Kram 0.11 now explains the conflict instead of failing in rpm; dnf swap kram kram-gtk switches to it.
On GNOME, a GTK 4 and libadwaita front end, kram-gtk, with the package list, menus, preferences and every dialog of the Qt one.
Switch between the front ends with dnf swap kram-qt kram-gtk, and back; the settings and the tray icon stay as they are.
The kram package is now kram-qt and kram-common; dnf upgrade replaces it and keeps the tray icon on.
About shows which front end and toolkit version is running.
The painted status and origin icons are sharp at fractional screen scales (125 %, 150 %).
On GNOME, Kram turns light or dark along with the desktop, in libadwaita's colours.
The Apply button works again.
If Kram is closed or crashes during a transaction, the transaction now finishes instead of stopping halfway.
Apply and Refresh can no longer start twice while dependencies are being resolved.
The administrator password is asked for each time Kram makes changes.
A package whose signature could not be checked is no longer shown as unsigned.
History and undo fixes, faster marking of many packages, and correct plural forms in translations.
File → Transaction History shows what dnf installed, upgraded and removed, and when; Mark Changes to Undo takes a transaction back, for review before Apply.
Package → Show in History lists the transactions that changed a package.
An Environments view in the sidebar (KDE Plasma Workspaces, Fedora Workstation, …), each unfolding into its groups.
Groups and environments are installed, upgraded or removed at once from their menu, after the review; optional packages are shown and can be installed.
The review checks free disk space and warns before removing the desktop you are using.
Refresh the metadata of a single repository from the Origin view.
Kernel upgrades are no longer shown as upgrades that cannot be installed, and Mark All Upgrades marks them again.
Status → Cannot be upgraded now lists the upgrades dnf leaves out, and the Dependencies tab says why.
The Dependencies tab of kernel-core no longer freezes the window.
Lock a package at its installed version (Package → Lock Version) and unlock it again.
A padlock marks locked packages, and the upgrade a lock holds back is shown greyed.
Status → Locked versions lists the locked packages.
An optional Download size column in the package list.
Export the listed packages as CSV (File menu).
An empty package list says why and links to what would fill it.
F5 reloads, as Ctrl+R does.
The Files tab of the package details shows the files in a folder tree or as a list.
A filter in the Files tab, with the matched text in bold.
Copy a file's path or show it in the file manager from the Files tab.
In the progress dialog, dnf's error messages appear in your language where dnf has a translation.
Kram's own messages in the progress dialog are translated too, such as the dnf5 command being run.
An upgrade that cannot be installed now shows a red cross before its version.
The Dependencies tab of such an upgrade shows why it cannot be installed.
The "Security updates" and "Bug fix updates" filters are hidden when there are none.
Kram builds again for Fedora Rawhide.
The Packages column of the Repositories and COPR dialogs counts distinct packages instead of every built version.
Repositories: Show packages filters the list to a repository's packages, and Remove deletes a repository you added yourself.
The Origin filters list each Fedora repository on its own.
Cleanup (formerly Package Cache) lists the leftover .rpmnew and .rpmsave configuration files, compares them with the current file and deletes them.
Mark Unneeded Dependencies for Removal marks what dnf autoremove would remove.
The Repository column shows where an installed package came from when its latest version is in another repository.
Upgrades that cannot be installed now (such as a new build that needs a missing library) are no longer counted by the update notifier.
The package list shows such upgrades dimmed, with the reason in the tooltip, and Mark All Upgrades leaves them out.
After a transaction, Kram waits for another package manager (such as akmods building kernel modules) instead of failing to load the package list.
The update check no longer fails while another package manager is running.
The Apply changes dialog says which marked upgrades cannot be installed and why, and Apply is disabled when nothing is left to do.
Packaging: the package builds again for Fedora Rawhide.
Updates: a coloured dot and an Update type column show which upgrades fix security issues (by severity), bugs or add enhancements.
Updates: an Advisories tab shows what an upgrade fixes, with links to the advisory, the bugs and the CVEs.
Updates: the sidebar lists the security updates and the bug fix updates on their own.
Updates: the arrow next to Mark All Upgrades marks only the security upgrades, only the critical and important ones, or the security and bug fix upgrades.
Custom filters: filter by update type.
Tray: clicking the update icon no longer crashes Kram when the icon appeared right after login.
Groups: right-click a group to install it, or to upgrade or remove an installed one.
Groups: Upgrade is offered only for groups that have something to upgrade.
Apply changes: groups and the packages they install or remove are listed separately.
Speed: the window no longer freezes for seconds when the cursor lands on a kernel package.
Speed: Provides searches by part of a name or with * are about 20 times faster and keep the window responsive.
Speed: typing a search and clearing it are several times faster in long package lists.
Speed: moving through the list no longer stalls on loading package details.
Sidebar: groups show icons from the system icon theme, and installed groups are in bold.
Sidebar: every Status entry has an icon matching the package list's status column.
Package files: opening an .rpm file no longer fails with "cannot create directories: Permission denied".
Update notifications: the tray icon appears right after Kram's Reload finds updates, and after waking from sleep.
Updates that change a package's architecture (noarch to x86_64, like python3-wcwidth in Fedora 45) now show the new version and install.
Xfce: Kram is in the Settings Manager (System section), as "Package Manager".
Fixed a rare crash after Kram finished loading packages or applying changes.
The tray icon shows the update level right after installing Kram, without restarting the Plasma panel.
An optional icon in the system tray while updates are available, with how many of them are security updates (Settings → Update Notifications). It downloads nothing: Fedora's own update check does.
Clicking the icon opens Kram on the upgradable packages.
Kram opens only once: starting it again brings the open window to the front.
Update Notifications can turn on Fedora's automatic update check, and turn off the update notifier of Discover or GNOME Software.
An option in Settings makes a click on the status icon mark the likely action (install, upgrade or unmark) instead of opening the menu.
The Mark All Upgrades icon no longer looks disabled when there are upgrades to mark.
Repositories: the id and the file path are shown in full, every column can be resized and the list scrolls sideways.
Repositories: right-click a file path to copy it or show it in the file manager.
The apply dialog no longer warns that an essential package is removed when only the oldest kernel makes room for a new one; those removals are listed apart.
Package names in the apply dialog are no longer cut short by long versions.
A toolbar button tells when a new Fedora release is out (Settings → Watch Fedora Releases, checked on Reload).
Its dialog works out what the upgrade would block, remove and need, and which COPR projects have no build for it, without changing anything. The upgrade itself stays with Discover or GNOME Software.
The progress bar keeps moving while waiting for a slow server, instead of sitting at 100%.
Custom filters have a new "Provides" condition, e.g. application() for packages with a menu entry.
The equivalent command in the apply dialog changes with "Download packages only".
Settings → Package Cache shows how much space the package caches take and where they are, and cleans them, including the packages Discover and GNOME Software downloaded and left behind.
Repositories and COPR are greyed out until the package list has loaded, instead of doing nothing.
The progress window stays on top of the COPR dialog that started it.
The progress window no longer says "Waiting for authentication" while metadata downloads.

Install a downloaded .rpm file (File → Open Package File…, drop it on the window, or "Open with Kram" in the file manager). Before anything happens it shows whether this installs, upgrades, downgrades or reinstalls, who signed the file, the scripts it runs as root, what satisfies each dependency and whether a repository has a newer version. A reinstall first checks the installed files.
Choose which recommended packages to install, with the size each one adds.
When another package operation is running, Kram says so instead of reporting a signature error.
Replacing a package is no longer logged as removing it, and the progress bar counts packages.
The apply dialog's columns fit their contents and widen with the window.
About → What's New lists the changes of every version.
Toolbar: a monochrome icon for Mark All Upgrades; Properties moved to the Package menu only.
The package details pane can no longer be collapsed out of sight.
Marking a package for removal offers to mark the packages that depend on it as well; before, applying such a removal failed.
A new column shows why each installed package is there (installed by the user, as a dependency, …).
Columns of the package list can be hidden from the header's context menu.

description.p: Kram is now released under the MIT License.

ul.li: Searches can be removed from the search history, or the whole history cleared.
The search field shows a funnel icon while its text filters the package list.

description.p: The package list loads even when an enabled repository cannot be loaded; such repositories are shown in the status bar.
Kram is now available in Czech, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Simplified Chinese and Spanish.
The progress dialog counts packages correctly and no longer logs each package twice.
Fixes "Permission denied" when loading the package catalog after a background metadata refresh.
Reload now shows newly published packages and the real metadata age. Custom filters in the sidebar, a compact toolbar style, and sharp icons on scaled screens.
First release: browse, search, mark and apply; repositories and COPR projects.
